items.title_en: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
items.title_zh: HiSTEVE 1.0：利用人机接口 VLA 智能体玩转开放世界游戏
items.abstract_en: Building virtual embodied agents that operate in open-ended games like human players is a long-standing goal requiring both long-horizon autonomy and reliable native-interface control. As a procedurally generated open world, Minecraft provides a natural testbed for studying the integration of these capabilities. Existing agents typically provide either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning executed through environment APIs or predefined skills. To bridge this gap, we propose HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness. At the orchestration level, we equip the harness with structured memory for tracking progress and a VLM planner for selecting subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. To reliably determine subtask completion, we further introduce a policy-coupled task completion state detector that conditions on VLA policy context to signal candidate completion. At the control level, a single VLA executes all subtasks with vision-only perception and native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between heterogeneous GUI and non-GUI interactions, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings. We also train the VLA through world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with environment feedback to improve reliability and recovery. HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, while also completing long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch like human players.
items.abstract_zh: 构建像人类玩家一样在开放式游戏中行动的虚拟具身智能体，既需要长时程自主性，也需要可靠的原始界面控制。Minecraft 作为程序生成的开放世界，为研究二者结合提供了天然试验场。现有智能体要么具备原生视觉运动控制但缺乏长时程自主性，要么通过环境 API 或预定义技能执行高层规划。为此我们提出 HiSTEVE：一种带能力感知外壳的分层 VLA 智能体。编排层配备用于跟踪进度的结构化记忆，以及只在 VLA 能力范围内选择子任务的 VLM 规划器，并引入策略耦合的任务完成状态检测器判定子任务完成；控制层由单个 VLA 以纯视觉感知和原生键鼠操作执行全部子任务，并通过分模式 RMSNorm 分支与独立鼠标移动 token 嵌入缓解 GUI 与非 GUI 交互的干扰。VLA 经世界知识注入、模仿学习与强化学习训练。HiSTEVE 在 MineStudio Bench 上得分 85.0%，在 OpenHA 上平均成功率 37.4%，并能像玩家一样从零制作铁镐。
items.highlight_zh: 分层 VLA 加能力感知外壳，纯键鼠在 Minecraft 完成长时程任务
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：让 AI 像人一样“玩”Minecraft 这类开放世界游戏，难点有两层：既要长时间自主地推进目标（长时程自主性），又要像人一样直接看屏幕、敲键盘点鼠标（原生界面控制）。此前工作常顾此失彼——能操作键鼠的只能做短任务，能规划长任务的却靠调用环境 API 或预定义技能，等于“作弊”。

2) 方法：作者把系统分成上下两层。上层“编排器”用结构化记忆记录已做到哪一步，再由视觉语言模型（VLM）规划器挑选下一个子任务，且只挑底层 VLA 确实会做的任务；为判断子任务是否完成，设计了与策略耦合的完成状态检测器，参考 VLA 自身上下文触发完成信号。下层是单个 VLA，仅凭画面输入直接输出键盘鼠标动作；由于 GUI 操作与游戏内操作风格迥异、易互相干扰，网络中加入分模式的归一化分支和单独的鼠标移动 token。

3) 训练：先注入世界知识，再做模仿学习，最后用环境反馈做强化学习，让智能体出错后能恢复。

4) 结果：在 MineStudio Bench 原子任务上得分 85.0%，在 OpenHA 上平均成功率 37.4%，并能像玩家一样从零砍树挖矿一路造出铁镐。

5) 意义：它把“看得懂、会规划、真动手”三件事缝合进一个原生键鼠接口的开放世界，为通用游戏智能体与具身智能体提供了可复用范式。

rm.usage: Minecraft 里靠键鼠操作的长时程具身智能体，与 RoboMaster 的云台自瞄、导航决策等任务形态差别很大，分层规划+能力感知的思路至多对哨兵长时程任务编排有一点点启发，实操上基本用不上。

items.title_en: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
items.title_zh: RynnUnify：迈向统一的具身大脑
items.abstract_en: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano. Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks. Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.
items.abstract_zh: 我们提出 RynnUnify，一个 16B 的统一具身模型，通过交错的视频—语言推理把强具身理解与长时程视觉规划结合起来。其能力涵盖空间推理、物理预测与 grounding，将理解物理世界与预判世界如何随子任务演变的视觉能力连接起来。在此基础上，我们通过强化学习开发了智能体式扩展，使其选择性使用视频预测推理未观测状态与交互结果；并开发了世界—动作扩展，把理解与预测能力转化为机器人控制。我们还提出 Rynn-VP 与 Rynn-GEU 两个基准，分别评估长时程视觉规划与前瞻推理。实验显示，RynnUnify 在所评估的统一多模态模型中具身理解平均得分最高，Rynn-VP 总分比 Cosmos 3 Nano 高 9.75 分；智能体扩展使 Rynn-GEU 平均分比直接推理提高 6.0 分；世界—动作扩展在 20 个选定 RoboCasa365 复合任务上成功率 51.5%，在三个真实机器人任务上平均成功率 46.7%。
items.highlight_zh: 16B 统一具身模型：理解、视频预测与机器人控制共用一个大脑
items.digest_zh:
1) 要解决的问题：机器人在真实世界干活，需要“看懂世界”和“预判接下来会怎样”两套能力，但现有模型往往只擅长其一。作者想造一个“统一具身大脑”，把理解、预测与控制装进同一个模型。

2) 方法：RynnUnify 参数量 16B，用交错的视频—语言序列做推理，也就是一边生成未来画面、一边用语言进行推理。它具备空间推理、物理预测以及 grounding（把语言指到画面中的具体物体）等能力。在此基础上作者做了两个扩展：一是用强化学习训练“智能体式”用法，让模型自己决定何时调用视频预测来推断看不到的状态和交互后果；二是“世界—动作”扩展，把理解与预测能力接到机器人动作上。

3) 评测：现有基准不够用，作者新建了 Rynn-VP（长时程视觉规划）与 Rynn-GEU（前瞻推理）。

4) 结果：在同类统一多模态模型中具身理解平均分最高；Rynn-VP 总分比 Cosmos 3 Nano 高 9.75 分；智能体式扩展让 Rynn-GEU 平均分提升 6.0 分；世界—动作版本在 20 个 RoboCasa365 复合任务上成功率为 51.5%，三个真实机器人任务平均成功率为 46.7%。

5) 意义：说明“先想清楚未来画面、再决定怎么动”的路线在统一模型里可行，为理解—规划—控制一体的具身基础模型提供了雏形。

rm.usage: 统一的视频-语言具身大脑与长时程视觉规划，可借鉴到哨兵机器人或多机战术决策的“预测对手未来状态+选子任务”设计，但模型规模 16B、面向机械臂控制，直接迁移到 RM 不现实。
rm.task: 哨兵机器人自主导航与决策

items.title_en: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
items.title_zh: HoloBoxing：单 GPU 训练 7 分钟的人形机器人拳击简易配方
items.abstract_en: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution. A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control. This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run. This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.
items.abstract_zh: HoloBoxing 提出一种基于预训练全身控制器的人形机器人拳击学习配方。该配方把可复用的运动技能与任务决策分离：一个紧凑的规划器输出未来身体点目标，冻结的控制器负责关节级执行。一个学习到的解码器把 32 维动作映射为结构化目标窗口，先用实测状态模仿来初始化规划器，再用强化学习细化交互行为，全程复用解码器与控制器，无需重新学习全身控制。这一组合使任务优化集中于紧凑的上层策略，并在奖励驱动的探索前提供初始行为。在已有控制器基础上，该配方只需约七分钟额外训练（含复用表征拟合与单 GPU 任务运行），不含控制器预训练、数据准备、评估与搜索。仿真拳击实验与组件对照实验评估了所得行为，以及模仿初始化与目标表征的作用。
items.highlight_zh: 解耦运动与决策，7 分钟单卡训练出人形拳击策略
items.digest_zh:
1) 问题：训练人形机器人打拳击这类需要全身协调的动作，通常要在仿真里从头学习全身控制，代价高、周期长。作者问：能不能把“会动”和“会打”拆开，让任务学习变得极轻量？

2) 方法：HoloBoxing 复用已有的预训练全身控制器并冻结它，只训练一个紧凑的上层规划器。规划器输出 32 维动作，经一个学到的解码器映射为结构化的身体目标点窗口，再由冻结控制器转成关节指令。训练分两步：先用实测状态做模仿，给规划器一个靠谱的起点；再用强化学习优化交互行为。解码器与控制器全程复用，不必重新学习全身控制。

3) 结果：在已有控制器前提下，任务训练只需约 7 分钟单 GPU 时间（含表征拟合与一次任务运行）；作者明确排除了控制器预训练、数据准备、评估与超参搜索的耗时。仿真拳击实验加消融对照，验证了行为有效，并说明模仿初始化与目标表征各自的作用。

4) 意义：它提示了一条“技能复用 + 轻量任务适配”的机器人学习流水线：底层运动能力一次训好反复使用，上层任务策略几分钟就能训出来，显著降低新任务门槛。

rm.usage: 人形机器人拳击的上层规划器+冻结全身控制器分离训练配方，与 RM 的轮式底盘/云台控制体系不同，仅其“紧凑上层策略+复用底层控制器”的训练范式对强化学习仿真有参考价值。

items.title_en: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
items.title_zh: Echo：面向视觉—语言—动作模型的耦合动作与任务状态信号去噪
items.abstract_en: Recognizing task completion and failure enables robots to stop upon success and initiate recovery or replanning after failure. Existing methods augment Vision Language Action (VLA) policies with task status signal prediction to support these execution decisions. However, learning and integrating these signals can require fine-grained supervision, external monitoring models, or complex architectural designs. Moreover, the potential of task status signals to directly guide action generation remains underexplored. We present Echo, a framework that combines task status signal learning without frame-level progress annotations with a compact design for status prediction and action generation within a single VLA. Specifically, Echo represents task status with stop and failure signals, added as two dimensions of each action chunk and denoised together with robot actions. Their combination distinguishes ongoing execution, successful completion, and failure. To learn these signals without fine-grained progress annotations, Echo constructs successful, failed, and recovery trajectories with complementary supervision properties. To enable status signal-guided action generation, Echo controls interactions between the signals and actions and denoises the signals faster than the actions. These allow later action denoising steps to condition on cleaner status estimates while preserving accurate signal prediction. Extensive real-world manipulation experiments show that Echo accurately predicts task status and consistently improves policy performance.
items.abstract_zh: 识别任务完成与失败，能让机器人在成功时停止、失败后恢复或重规划。现有方法为 VLA 策略增加任务状态信号预测来支持这些执行决策，但学习与整合这些信号往往需要细粒度监督、外部监控模型或复杂架构，且状态信号直接引导动作生成的潜力仍未被充分挖掘。我们提出 Echo：一个无需帧级进度标注即可学习任务状态信号，并在单个 VLA 内以紧凑设计同时完成状态预测与动作生成的框架。Echo 用停止与失败信号表示任务状态，将其作为每个动作块的两个维度与机器人动作一起去噪，二者组合可区分执行中、成功完成与失败。为在无细粒度标注下学习信号，Echo 构建了具有互补监督性质的成对成功、失败与恢复轨迹；为使状态信号引导动作生成，Echo 控制信号与动作的交互，并让信号比动作更快去噪，使后续动作去噪步骤可基于更干净的状态估计，同时保持信号预测准确。大量真实机器人操作实验表明 Echo 能准确预测任务状态，并稳定提升策略性能。
items.highlight_zh: 停止/失败信号与动作一起去噪，无需进度标注即可增强 VLA
items.digest_zh:
1) 问题：机器人执行任务时若不知道自己做没做完、有没有失败，就只能一直做下去。已有做法是给 VLA（视觉—语言—动作模型）额外加一个“任务状态”预测头，但往往要帧级进度标注、外挂监控模型或复杂结构；而且这些状态信号能否反过来指导动作生成，此前没人深挖。

2) 方法：Echo 的思路很简洁——把“停止”和“失败”两个状态信号直接当作动作块里多出来的两个维度，与机器人动作一起做扩散去噪。一次前向即可同时得到动作与状态，两者组合可区分“还在做”“成功完成”“失败”。为免去帧级标注，作者构造了成功、失败、恢复三类轨迹，利用它们互补的监督性质来学习信号。更关键的是去噪节奏：让状态信号比动作去噪得更快，后续动作去噪步骤就能参考更干净的状态估计，同时不牺牲信号本身的预测精度。

3) 结果：在大量真实机器人操作实验中，Echo 能准确预测任务状态，并稳定提升策略成功率。

4) 意义：它表明任务状态不只是事后的“裁判”，还能当动作生成的“向导”；而且这种改造几乎没有额外结构成本，容易嫁接到现有 VLA 上。

rm.usage: 把任务完成/失败信号与动作一起去噪、无需帧级进度标注，可迁移到工程机器人视觉装配的成功判定与失败重试逻辑（如判断模块是否装入能量单元），但需替换为 RM 的视觉伺服策略。

items.title_en: DriveOSS: Dataset and Benchmark for 3D Anomaly Segmentation and Open-set Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Driving
items.title_zh: DriveOSS：面向自动驾驶中三维异常分割与开放集语义分割的数据集与基准
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in 3D semantic segmentation have significantly improved scene understanding in autonomous driving. However, existing methods are typically developed under a closed-set assumption and evaluated under standard driving conditions, where all categories are known in advance. In real-world driving, autonomous vehicles inevitably encounter previously unseen objects, making closed-set perception insufficient for safe deployment. To address this challenge, we introduce DriveOSS, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first real-world multimodal dataset and benchmark specifically designed for 3D anomaly segmentation and open-set semantic segmentation. It contains 12,661 synchronized and annotated frames captured using six surround-view RGB cameras, a 128-beam LiDAR, and a GPS/IMU unit. The dataset comprises 52 real-world driving scenes collected under clear, nighttime, cloudy, rainy, and snowy conditions and is organized into ID (in-distribution) and OOD (out-of-distribution) subsets. The ID scenes contain only known classes and are used for training, whereas the OOD scenes additionally contain unknown objects annotated as the outlier class and are used for validation and testing. Extensive experiments show that unseen objects remain a major challenge for current 3D perception systems. The dataset, benchmark protocols, and code are available at https://github.com/chrisyan/DriveOSS.
items.abstract_zh: 现有三维语义分割方法多在闭集假设与标准驾驶条件下开发与评测，而真实驾驶中不可避免会遇到从未见过的物体，闭集感知难以支撑安全部署。为此，作者提出 DriveOSS，这是首个面向三维异常分割与开放集语义分割的真实世界多模态数据集与基准。该数据集包含 12,661 帧同步且带标注的数据，由 6 路环视 RGB 相机、128 线 LiDAR 与 GPS/IMU 采集，覆盖晴、夜、多云、雨、雪五种天气下的 52 个真实驾驶场景，并划分为两个子集：ID（分布内）子集仅含已知类别，用于训练；OOD（分布外）子集额外包含被标注为离群类的未知物体，用于验证与测试。大量实验表明，未见物体仍是当前三维感知系统面临的主要挑战。
items.highlight_zh: 首个面向自动驾驶三维异常与开放集语义分割的真实多模态基准
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：自动驾驶的感知模型通常假设“所有类别事先已知”，但真实道路上一定会出现没见过的物体（如异形车辆、掉落货物）。这类情况会让闭集模型把未知物误判成已知类别，带来安全隐患。但目前缺少专门评测“识别未知物”能力的真实数据集。

方法与数据：作者构建了 DriveOSS。他们用 6 路环视相机、128 线 LiDAR 和 GPS/IMU 同步采集了 12,661 帧数据，覆盖晴天、夜间、多云、雨雪等不同天气与光照下的 52 个真实驾驶场景。数据被分成两半性质不同的部分：ID 子集只含已知类别，用于训练模型；OOD 子集额外包含未知物体，并统一标注为“离群类”，用于验证和测试。这样就能直接衡量模型能否把未知物从已知类别中区分出来。

结果：作者在数据集上跑了大量现有三维感知方法的实验，结论是：未见物体依然是当前系统的一大短板，现有方法在开放场景下表现明显下降。

为何重要：它把“开放世界感知”从概念讨论变成了可复现的公开基准，提供统一的数据、评测协议与代码，让研究者能公平比较不同方法识别未知物体的能力，推动自动驾驶感知从闭集走向开放集，对安全部署有直接意义。

rm.usage: 开放集三维语义分割与异常检测基准，思路可用于雷达站激光点云感知：在闭集训练下识别未见过目标/异常点云，提升雷达对敌方机器人及遮挡异常的检出鲁棒性；但数据域是车载驾驶，需自建标注。
rm.task: 雷达目标探测与信息融合

items.title_en: VERA-Hand: A Verified Multidimensional Benchmark for 2D Hand Pose Estimation in Third-Person Dynamic Gesture Videos
items.title_zh: VERA-Hand：面向第三人称动态手势视频二维手部姿态估计的经人工核验多维基准
items.abstract_en: Hand landmarks serve as input for gesture recognition, sign language understanding, and touchless human-computer interaction. Yet hand pose estimators are typically evaluated with frame-wise localization metrics such as PCK or MPJPE, which are computed over matched predictions and overlook missed or spurious hands, handedness errors, and temporal instability. To address these limitations, we present VERA-Hand, a benchmark that evaluates estimators using manually verified, frame-level 2D annotations for 10,690 hands across four complementary dimensions (detection, localization, identification, and temporal stability), as well as a joint Pose-F1 metric that requires both correct detection and accurate localization. Evaluating six estimators spanning hand-specific, whole-body, reconstruction-based, and foundation-model paradigms, we find that no estimator dominates: rankings reorder sharply across dimensions. VERA-Hand also exposes failures that localization-only and downstream evaluations may not reveal, including cross-hand overlap in over 85% of frames for a recent foundation model. A post-hoc cleanup case study demonstrates how the benchmark can validate corrective interventions, while stratified analyses show that robustness varies across motion-blur classes and hand regions. We release the verified annotations, protocol, and code at https://gibranbenitez.github.io/VERA_Hand/
items.abstract_zh: 手部关键点是手势识别、手语理解与无接触人机交互的基础输入，但手部姿态估计器通常只用 PCK、MPJPE 等逐帧定位指标评测，且只统计匹配上的预测，忽略漏检、虚检、左右手判定错误与时间抖动。为此，作者提出 VERA-Hand 基准：基于人工核验的逐帧二维标注，对 10,690 只手从检测、定位、识别、时间稳定性四个互补维度进行评测，并提出需同时满足正确检测与准确定位的联合指标 Pose-F1。评测覆盖手部专用、全身、重建式与基础模型四类共六个估计器，发现没有哪个估计器全面占优，各维度排名差异明显。该基准还揭示出仅看定位或下游任务难以发现的失败，例如某近期基础模型在超过 85% 的帧中出现左右手重叠。
items.highlight_zh: 提出四维手部姿态评测基准，揭示定位指标看不到的失败
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：手部关键点检测是手势识别、手语翻译、隔空交互等任务的前置环节。然而现有评测几乎只看“关键点位置准不准”（如 PCK、MPJPE），而且只在成功匹配的预测上计算。这会掩盖三类真实问题：根本没检测到手、把背景误检成手、左右手搞反，以及视频中关键点来回抖动。

方法：作者构建了 VERA-Hand 基准，用人工逐帧核验的二维标注覆盖 10,690 只手，从四个互补维度打分：能否检测到（检测）、位置是否准确（定位）、左右手是否判对（识别）、视频中是否稳定（时间稳定性）。此外还设计了联合指标 Pose-F1，只有“检测对且定位准”才算通过，避免单一指标虚高。评测对象包括手部专用模型、全身姿态模型、基于重建的方法和通用基础模型，共六个估计器。

结果：没有任何一个估计器在所有维度上领先，换个维度排名就会大洗牌；某些模型虽然在定位指标上表现不错，但会出现严重的左右手混淆——某近期基础模型在超过 85% 的帧里两只手区域重叠。分层分析还显示，鲁棒性会随运动模糊程度和手部区域不同而变化。

为何重要：它说明“关键点很准”不等于“手部感知可靠”，为手势与手语等下游应用提供了更贴近实际需求的多维评测标准。作者还通过一个事后修正的案例，证明该基准可以用来检验改进手段是否真的有效，并公开了标注、协议与代码。

rm.usage: 第三人称手势/手部关键点估计基准，与装甲板点阵识别、能量机关灯臂检测等任务的目标形态无关，仅其“检测+定位+时间稳定性”联合评价指标可借用来评估自瞄跟踪的时序稳定性。

items.title_en: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
items.title_zh: SCOPE：面向机器人长期规划数据集的计划误差校正优化场景图构建
items.abstract_en: Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) stands as a fundamental challenge in robotics, essential for enabling autonomous agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks in diverse environments. While Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce a new paradigm for TAMP by leveraging extensive common sense, their inherent reasoning limitations hinder direct application, and fine-tuning strategies to enhance these capabilities are currently bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing automated generation methods often suffer from homogeneity, limiting model generalization, and unsolvability, where hallucinated scene graphs create physical mismatches with task goals. To address these issues, we propose Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets. SCOPE incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios. Crucially, it introduces a Plan Feedback Error-correction pipeline that utilizes planner execution failures as feedback signals to retroactively rectify logical inconsistencies in scene graphs, ensuring physical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that SCOPE exhibits greater robustness to erroneous scene graphs and generates higher-quality data. When utilized for LLM fine-tuning, SCOPE-generated data yield a downstream TAMP model that achieves an absolute 12.33% gain in success rate over its counterpart fine-tuned with data generated by DELTA, a state-of-the-art PDDL-based planner.
items.comment: 8 pages. Accepted at IROS 2026. Project page: https://scope-page.github.io/

rm.usage: 面向 TAMP 的场景图与计划误差校正数据生成，可类比用于工程机器人装配任务的长期任务规划数据构造，但场景与动作空间差异大，对 RM 核心环节帮助有限。

items.title_en: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation
items.title_zh: RoboJudge：多模态语言模型作为具身视频生成的评判者
items.abstract_en: Video generation models are promising foundations for embodied world models, but only if their generated rollouts are physically valid and faithful to task instructions. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to judge these properties, yet their agreement with human judgments on embodied videos has not been systematically evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as judges of embodied video generation. The benchmark measures two fundamental dimensions, Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, across 800 human-annotated videos from 8 source corpora and 10 video generators, spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Experiments reveal uneven alignment between existing judges and human ratings: general-purpose MLLMs show lower agreement on physical adherence, while specialized video judges designed for general-domain physical reasoning do not consistently transfer to embodied scenarios. Motivated by these findings, we construct RoboJudge-Train, comprising 12K videos annotated with 25K human-verified scores and model-assisted rationales for Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment. We fine-tune a 9B MLLM on this dataset with supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, yielding RoboJudge-9B. Among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench, RoboJudge-9B achieves the highest overall agreement, reaching a Pearson correlation of 0.719 with a statistically significant 0.089 gain over Gemini-3.7-Flash, the best-performing proprietary baseline in our evaluation. Training on RoboJudge-Train also yields gains on external benchmarks, including VideoPhy2 and Physion-Eval. We further use RoboJudge-9B as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment.

rm.usage: 用多模态大模型评判具身视频生成的物理合理性与指令一致性，可作为 RM 仿真/世界模型生成对抗轨迹时的自动评测工具，辅助自瞄、导航策略的仿真验证，属支撑性工具。

items.title_en: Unified Trajectory and 3D Pose Forecasting for Multi-Agent Sports Analysis
items.title_zh: 面向多智能体体育分析的统一轨迹与3D姿态预测
items.abstract_en: Forecasting future human motion requires jointly reasoning about an agent's global trajectory and 3D body pose, which are tightly coupled, particularly in team sports where multiple interacting players introduce complex social dynamics. We exploit a socio-temporal encoder that fuses trajectory and pose at the input level and models them jointly through shared factorized attention. The model is further enhanced by a per-joint loss reweighting scheme that emphasizes dynamic joints and prevents degenerate solutions, and a frequency-domain trajectory smoothing term that improves trajectory prediction while indirectly benefiting pose forecasting. To ensure fair comparison with prior joint forecasting methods, we identify and correct evaluation biases arising from overlapping sequence construction, adopting instead a non-overlapping protocol and a deterministic, oracle-free strategy for multi-future prediction. Our approach improves over prior joint forecasting methods on both WorldPose and 3DPW, with the largest gains on pose accuracy, demonstrating that the proposed joint formulation generalizes beyond the densely interactive scenarios that motivate it.

rm.usage: 多智能体轨迹与姿态联合预测的思路可迁移到雷达/哨兵中，用历史位置序列预测敌方多台机器人的未来运动轨迹，辅助预判和拦截；但其3D人体姿态部分与RM无关，需大幅改造。
rm.task: 雷达目标探测与信息融合

items.title_en: MDMR-Bench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Multi-Reference Image Generation
items.title_zh: MDMR-Bench：多参考图像生成的多维基准
items.abstract_en: Image generation models have rapidly advanced, with many models now supporting generation conditioned on multiple reference images and textual instructions. Such models enable a wide range of applications, including entity fusion and attribute transfer across images. However, existing benchmarks for multi-reference image generation rely on limited evaluation dimensions and fail to capture the diverse challenges of the task. To address this limitation, we propose MDMR-Bench, a Multi-Dimensional benchmark for Multi-Reference image generation. MDMR-Bench is organized around representative capability settings and consists of multiple evaluation subsets spanning diverse dimensions of multi-reference image generation, including (1) common entity fusion and attribute transfer, (2) multi-element extraction from a single image, (3) infographic manipulation, and (4) visual reasoning-intensive generation. This design enables systematic analysis of model capabilities and failure modes across different challenge dimensions. Furthermore, to achieve more reliable and interpretable evaluation, we introduce a checklist-based evaluation protocol that decomposes generation quality into fine-grained evaluation aspects. Instead of relying solely on holistic scoring, our framework uses structured checklists composed of both global-level and atomic-level queries, enabling more diagnostic assessment of model performance. By benchmarking both open-source and proprietary models, we demonstrate that MDMR-Bench provides fine-grained insights into model performance across different dimensions. The dataset and code are publicly available.
items.comment: Bowen Zheng and Jintao Lin contributed equally to this work. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track

items.title_en: Joint-Angle Invariance of Jacobian-Based Performance Indices for Serial Robotic Manipulators
items.title_zh: 串联机器人机械臂基于雅可比性能指标的关节角不变性
items.abstract_en: This article investigates the joint-angle invariance (JAI) of Jacobian-based performance indices for serial robotic manipulators. We identify kinematic conditions under which representative performance indices, including manipulability, stiffness, and other Jacobian-derived indices, remain independent of the first and last joint angles. This property allows a systematic reduction in the effective configuration-space dimensionality, thereby simplifying the performance evaluation. The utility of JAI is demonstrated through two application scenarios: workspace performance map construction and task layout optimization. Comparative results show that the proposed JAI-based strategy reduces computational effort and storage requirements without compromising the effectiveness.
items.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at the 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026)

rm.usage: 雅可比性能指标（可操作度、刚度）的关节角不变性分析，可用于工程机器人机械臂的工作空间性能图构建与构型降维评估，属于离线设计阶段的支撑工具，需结合实际臂模型改造。

items.title_en: Preserving Operator Intent Under Actuation Constraints: Teleoperation of Manipulators with Coupled Transmissions
items.title_zh: 驱动约束下保持操作员意图：耦合传动机械臂的遥操作
items.abstract_en: Teleoperation enables intuitive control of remote engineering robots for precision tasks. Existing direct joint-mapping methods have two limitations: independent motor saturation disrupts pitch-roll coordination in differential wrists, while fixed mappings struggle with abrupt tracking changes caused by gravitational loads and actuation constraints. We propose an actuator-constraint-aware leader-follower teleoperation method that jointly models leader gravity compensation, leader-follower joint mapping, and follower differential-wrist control. Specifically, we perform coordinated saturation in motor space according to the available gravity margin and integrate continuous angle unwrapping, feedback-state monitoring, and feasible-reference updates. This preserves the operator's motion direction, reduces coordination distortion, and suppresses recovery transients during saturation or brief communication failures. Real-robot experiments demonstrate smoother wrist trajectories and more continuous recovery than direct mapping.
items.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Contribution to the IROS 2026 workshop "5th Sensorimotor-Augmented Teleoperation: Human-Interaction-Oriented Paradigm and Real-World Concerns"

rm.usage: 面向耦合传动机械臂的遥操作映射与饱和协调方法，可参考用于工程机器人机械臂操作端的关节映射与限幅处理，但RM工程以视觉自动装配为主，遥操作部分关联有限。

items.title_en: Distance Field Driven Reinforcement Learning for Reactive and Robust Collision Avoidance
items.title_zh: 距离场驱动的强化学习用于反应式与鲁棒避障
items.abstract_en: Robust and reactive collision avoidance remains a central challenge for deploying Reinforcement Learning (RL) policies on real robotic manipulators, particularly when transferring behaviours learned in simulation to the physical world. This paper presents an RL framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field (EDF) directly into the observation space, providing the agent with continuous geometric cues that support stable and responsive avoidance behaviours. By leveraging the rich spatial information encoded in the EDF, the method enables a streamlined reward formulation that achieves effective obstacle avoidance both with and without Artificial Potential Field guidance. The proposed approach is validated on a 7-DoF redundant manipulator, demonstrating zero-shot transfer from simulation to real hardware. Despite being trained exclusively with randomised static objects, the deployed policy generalizes to previously unseen real environments and exhibits robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles. These results highlight the potential of EDF-based representations to mitigate the sim-to-real gap and support reliable and real-time collision-aware behaviour in complex and changing environments.
items.comment: Accepted to 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

rm.usage: 把欧氏距离场放入观测空间做反应式避障的RL框架，可直接借鉴到哨兵自主导航的避障策略训练及仿真环境搭建，用距离场提供连续几何提示，简化奖励设计。

items.title_en: Media Intelligence Platform: Multimodal Detection of Synthetic and Manipulated Content
items.title_zh: 媒体智能平台：合成与篡改内容的多模态检测
items.abstract_en: The rapid progress of generative artificial intelligence has led to a significant increase in manipulated multimedia content, including synthetic faces, forged videos, AI-generated images, fake audio, and locally edited images. Existing detection approaches are typically designed for a single manipulation type, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios involving heterogeneous media sources. In this work, we present the Media Intelligence Platform (MIP), a unified web-based framework for multimodal media forensics integrating specialized modules for fake video detection, face morphing detection, AI-generated image detection, audio deepfake detection, localized image manipulation detection, and text analysis. Its modular architecture enables flexible integration of heterogeneous models and supports future extensions for emerging manipulation techniques. Experimental results on representative benchmark datasets demonstrate reliable detection performance across multiple media modalities while providing a practical and user-friendly interface for forensic investigations. The platform highlights the potential of unified multimodal systems for comprehensive deepfake detection in real-world environments, and is accompanied by a public demonstrator released with this workshop submission to support reproducibility and community evaluation.
items.comment: ECCV 2026, Workshop on AI for Multimedia Forensics & Disinformation Detection (AI4MFDD2026)

items.title_en: Effectiveness of Curriculum Learning Depends on Reward Sparsity and Competing Optima
items.title_zh: 课程学习的有效性取决于奖励稀疏性与竞争最优解
items.abstract_en: While animals and people tend to learn a task more quickly and reliably when they first train on simpler versions of it, curriculum learning's effectiveness in artificial settings varies, and appears substantially greater in reinforcement learning than in supervised learning. In this work, we construct and analyze a minimal model of policy learning to better understand why. We consider an open-loop, episodic target interception task whose parameters---especially how close the agent must be to the target to receive an informative reward signal---can be chosen so that the agent either receives informative rewards frequently ('dense' rewards) or rarely ('sparse' rewards). We mathematically and numerically analyze the dynamics of REINFORCE-based policy learning in both cases. In the dense reward case, curricula have only marginal benefits; in the sparse case, curricula can be required for learning to occur at all. We find that this is especially true when the agent has the conflicting goals of minimizing effort and accumulating high reward, since this can produce distinct reward landscape optima which compete with one another. Our characterization of useful curricula in this setting indicates that they address two issues: they (i) make rewards less sparse to speed up learning, and (ii) shape the reward landscape to steer agents away from bad local optima.

rm.usage: 关于课程学习在稀疏奖励与目标截获任务中有效性的分析，可用于仿真训练中为自瞄命中、拦截追击、战术决策等RL任务设计由易到难的课程与奖励阈值，属于训练方法论支撑。

items.title_en: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
items.title_zh: F2G-Pose：面向直接RGB-D类别级物体位姿估计的几何感知基础特征提升
items.abstract_en: This paper studies category-level RGB-D object pose estimation, which recovers an object's 3D rotation and translation without instance-specific CAD models or reference views. This task is highly ambiguous due to intra-class variations, symmetries, and partial observations. Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at https://jrryzh.github.io/F2G-Pose/.
items.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 22 pages, including the complete technical appendix

items.title_en: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control
items.title_zh: 用于实时分区控制中零样本协调的认知受限伙伴
items.abstract_en: Effective human-machine teaming requires agents that coordinate with unpredictable human partners. Reinforcement learning from live human feedback or large behavioural datasets is expensive, while purely simulated training overfits to artificial conventions and fails at Zero-Shot Coordination with real people. We propose a framework for training teaming agents against Cognitively Constrained Partners: simulated partners whose diversity emerges from procedural constraints grounded in human physiological literature, specifically reaction delays and perceptual limitations, rather than from reward shaping or historical training checkpoints. In a modified Lunar Lander environment, we report preliminary evidence that these partners play more like real people than unconstrained agents do, and that agents trained against them match the strongest cross-play baselines while being the only ones whose performance does not depend on how their training partners were generated. We also describe a human-participant study designed so that its rankings can be compared directly against cross-play, testing how well that standard evaluation predicts real human-agent teaming.
items.comment: 30 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Human-AI Coevolution: Measuring Human-Agent Teams in the Agentic Era

items.title_en: MINER: Modeling Inter- and Intra-Person Variance for Reidentification
items.title_zh: MINER：建模人际与个体内方差用于重识别
items.abstract_en: Clothes-Changing Person Re-Identification (CC-ReID) remains challenging due to drastic appearance shifts across outfits. Most prior works devise biometric signal-extraction heuristics to enhance inter-person variance, e.g., using segmentation masks, while leaving intra-person variance uncontrolled. We present MINER, a simple model-agnostic framework that suppresses garment bias by contrasting hard examples and adaptively balancing dataset-dependent intra- and inter-person variance. Extensive experiments show that MINER improves retrieval across CC-ReID benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on four datasets and ranking among the leaders in all three tracks of the open TVRID RGB-Depth ReID challenge.
items.comment: Paper accepted to the WACV 2027 Algorithms track

items.title_en: Depth-guided Geometric Adaptation for Few-shot Image Classification
items.title_zh: 深度引导的几何自适应用于小样本图像分类
items.abstract_en: Few-shot image classification (FSIC) frequently suffers from visual ambiguity, where background clutter and RGB appearance similarities hinder discriminative feature matching in data-scarce settings. To mitigate this, we propose DAFIC, a geometry-guided framework that incorporates monocular depth into representation learning, episodic adaptation, and dense support-query matching. DAFIC first learns geometry-aware token representations through RGB-D self-supervised pre-training. Subsequently, the Depth-guided Geometric Adaptation (DGA) module uses depth-derived geometry to refine patch representations with geometry-enriched class context while suppressing background interference. Spatial Bidirectional Patch Matching (SBiM) then performs bidirectional dense matching on the refined features, reducing sensitivity to spurious correspondences and background clutter. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks show that DAFIC achieves strong performance against existing methods, with ablation and robustness analyses supporting the effectiveness of coupling geometry-conditioned episodic adaptation with bidirectional matching for few-shot visual recognition.
items.comment: This work is accepted by The IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027

items.title_en: Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning
items.title_zh: 长描述在何处失效？面向细节图像描述的位置感知诊断与强化学习
items.abstract_en: Detailed image captioning is usually framed as an amount problem: a model should mention more visual facts while avoiding hallucination. However, autoregressive VLMs generate captions as ordered sequences, and later generations may be produced under weaker or noisier visual grounding. We therefore argue that long-form captioning should be studied not only by what facts are mentioned, but also by where they appear. We introduce a position-aware rubric representation that decomposes dense human references into atomic visual claims, verifies generated captions against those claims, and induces a quartile-wise composition of supported, hallucinated, and generic content. This lens reveals two qualitatively different failures in long captions: models tend to produce unsupported specificity in the middle, while the final portion often escapes into vague, non-evidential language rather than simply accumulating more hallucination. A same-reference human control does not exhibit these patterns; additional human audits examine the visual validity of the induced labels. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose PAGER (Position-Aware Grounded Evidence Reinforcement), a GRPO training objective with separate signals for supported fine-grained middle evidence, evidence-bearing tail continuation, claim coverage, and content-aware length control. The result is a closed loop: the same ordered claim representation identifies where long captions fail and supplies the position-specific reward needed to repair those failures. Experiments on detailed-caption benchmarks show that PAGER improves position-wise grounding and pairwise caption preference while preserving competitive global caption quality.
items.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 38 pages, 3 figures; includes references, appendices, and the paper checklist

items.title_en: RECAP: Looking Once Is Not Enough for Vision-Language Reasoning
items.title_zh: RECAP：看一眼并不足以支撑视觉-语言推理
items.abstract_en: Long chain-of-thought reasoning improves vision-language models (VLMs), but it also exposes a temporal grounding failure: as generation unfolds, models may drift from image evidence while reinforcement learning still provides only a final-answer reward. We study this gap through visual revisit, a temporally localized reactivation of image evidence during reasoning. Across three VLM backbones, revisit peaks are predictive of correctness and causally linked to performance: masking them degrades accuracy more than masking non-peaks, while injecting revisit-like peaks into failed rollouts partially restores correct answers. Control analyses show that this signal is not explained by raw attention strength, uncertainty, logit margin, or hidden-state norm. We propose RECAP, a GRPO-compatible training method that turns detached revisit traces into a credit-assignment signal. RECAP uses revisit-conditioned advantage estimation, dynamic discounting, and gated value prediction to propagate final rewards through visually important reasoning steps, without extra rewards, additional rollouts, or inference-time changes. Across Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, and LLaVA-OV-7B, RECAP consistently improves over GRPO and VPPO, yielding $+6.1$--$+6.5$ HallusionBench gains over the SFT base while preserving reasoning and text-only performance. Results on larger LoRA-tuned models, Chinese zero-shot benchmarks, visual perturbations, and human evaluation further demonstrate robust improvements in image-grounded reasoning.

items.title_en: DRILL: Training World Models to Improve Policies, Not Predict Pixels
items.title_zh: DRILL：训练世界模型以改进策略，而非预测像素
items.abstract_en: World models are increasingly used to reduce environment interaction when post-training vision-language-action (VLA) policies with reinforcement learning. Yet they are typically trained to predict pixels one step ahead, even though their role here is not merely to render visually faithful videos but to produce learning signals from imagined rollouts that improve the policy. We show that this mismatch is substantial: lower pixel MSE can produce worse policy gradients, and a world model trained for policy utility can yield better downstream policies despite 17% higher pixel MSE on the next frame. We propose the Downstream-Return Imagination Learning Loop (DRILL), a bilevel framework that updates the world model to maximize the policy's return after an inner GRPO update on imagined rollouts. DRILL has two instantiations. DRILL-VWI is a closed-form surrogate, requiring no additional simulator rollouts, that reweights prediction errors by policy visitation, the group-relative GRPO advantage, and model confidence. DRILL-IMG is a full meta-gradient method that differentiates through the inner update using truncated Hessian-vector products. We show that DRILL-VWI recovers the local one-step component of the DRILL-IMG meta-gradient under score-compatibility and small-residual assumptions. Across five manipulation simulators and two VLA backbones, DRILL-IMG raises mean success rate by 13.1 points over WMPO and 7.9 points over RLVR-World, and complements RLVR pretraining rather than competing with it. More broadly, we believe video world models for VLA reinforcement learning can be productively trained by the policy gradients they produce, not only by pixel-level prediction.

rm.usage: 以策略收益而非像素重建为目标训练世界模型，可用于仿真环节：在 sim 中构建决策/对抗世界模型以减少真实对局试错，提升强化学习训练效率。

items.title_en: FocusVLA: Future-Intent Guided Dynamic View Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.title_zh: FocusVLA：面向视觉-语言-动作模型的未来意图引导动态视角路由
items.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have become an important paradigm for robotic manipulation by unifying visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Since reliable manipulation requires sufficient observation of objects, end-effectors, and their spatial relationships, multi-view inputs are widely used to provide complementary spatial information. However, our experiments show that existing VLA models do not fully exploit such multi-view complementarity. The policy tends to persistently rely on the wrist view, lacking the ability to dynamically adjust global-local view dependency across manipulation stages, which limits stage adaptability and robustness. To address this issue, we propose FocusVLA, a stage-aware multi-view routing framework. FocusVLA predicts future interaction intent from historical actions and uses it to guide dynamic view routing during action generation. By adaptively coordinating global and local observations across different task stages, FocusVLA improves multi-view utilization. On RoboTwin 2.0, FocusVLA improves the average success rate over the strongest baseline $π_{0.5}$ by 10.10 pp. In real-world evaluation, FocusVLA improves the success rate from 71.7\% to 85.0\%, achieving a 13.3\% gain over $π_{0.5}$. Moreover, the intent prediction and dynamic routing modules of FocusVLA can be integrated into existing VLA frameworks without modifying their core architectures.

items.title_en: HATCH: Hardware-Attested Task Chains for Verifiable Manipulation
items.title_zh: HATCH：面向可验证操作的硬件认证任务链
items.abstract_en: Capability claims in robot manipulation are unverifiable, and existing leaderboards are each closed, simulated, or gameable. We propose HATCH, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark. Tasks span five skill categories at three difficulty levels and are chained so that the sensor confirming one task's completion unlocks the next, turning a room into a single long-horizon evaluation. Success is confirmed by instrumentation rather than human judgment, scoring is embodiment-agnostic, and object placements are randomized by a run-day seed. Entrants submit attested self-runs (uncut video, sensor logs, and the seed), with occasional organized events for calibration. Task specifications, build guide, bill of materials, and scoring rubrics are released under an open license.
items.comment: 2 pages, 1 table. Accepted at the 5th Workshop on Open Robotics Software, IROS 2026, Pittsburgh, PA, USA. Benchmark repository: https://github.com/shizacharania/hatch-benchmark

items.title_en: UniRAP: Towards Unified Part-level Physical Affordance Reasoning and Actionable Perception
items.title_zh: UniRAP：迈向统一的部件级物理可供性推理与可操作感知
items.abstract_en: Vision-language perception has achieved impressive progress in aligning natural language with visual observations, yet grounding high-level semantics into part-level physical interaction remains challenging. To address this gap, we propose UniRAP, a unified model for inferring part-level physical affordances and mapping language instructions to actionable geometric representations. UniRAP formulates this problem as a conditional multimodal generation task, integrating visual inputs, textual instructions, and optional prompts into a shared spatiotemporal representation space through a unified interface token mechanism. To predict executable contact geometry, we introduce a Unified Affordance Decoder (UAD), which jointly performs object detection, part-level affordance segmentation, and 4-DoF interaction pose estimation by leveraging intermediate segmentation features. In addition, we propose a curriculum-based transfer training strategy that progressively adapts the model from general visual parsing to interaction-aware perception, improving data efficiency under limited textual annotations. Experiments show that UniRAP achieves state-of-the-art performance on referring expression segmentation, affordance grounding, and interaction pose estimation, while maintaining strong spatiotemporal consistency in dynamic video scenarios. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of UniRAP as a unified perception framework for language-guided physical manipulation.

rm.usage: 部件级可供性推理可迁移到工程机器人的视觉装配环节：给定语言指令与RGB图，定位能量单元/42mm发射机构等部件的可抓取区域与操作位姿，辅助机械臂选择抓取点和装配动作。

items.title_en: Bio-inspired Thrust-Assisted Trotting on a legged-Aerial Robot via Real-Time QP-MPC
items.title_zh: 基于实时QP-MPC的仿生推力辅助腿足-空中机器人小跑运动
items.abstract_en: This paper presents the hardware implementation of a quadratic program-based controller on Harpy: thruster-assisted bipedal robot to perform thruster-assisted trotting. This is inspired by wing-assisted locomotion observed in birds such as the chukar partridge, which employ thrust vectoring to manipulate the ground reaction force. The proposed controller formulates the thruster-assisted spring-loaded inverted pendulum dynamics as a condensed QP-based model predictive control problem, enabling simultaneous regulation of ground contact force and active thrust vectoring at 500 Hz. A decoupled control architecture is used, where the robot's sagittal dynamics are controlled using QP-MPC while the frontal dynamics is regulated using a cascade orientation stabilization controller. Two experiments were conducted with different forward reference velocities of 0 m/s and 0.1 m/s. While the instantaneous velocity oscillates, the mean velocities can track their respective reference. Additionally, joint tracking error remains within 1 deg while tracking the desired leg length given by the leg trajectory controller and desired swing trajectory given by Raibert's heuristic. The QP-MPC problem is consistently solved with 0.18ms, which is well within the 2ms computation budget while satisfying the GRF friction cone constraint.
items.comment: To be published in IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026)

items.title_en: BIRD-RL: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning over Stateful Data-Centric Environments
items.title_zh: BIRD-RL：在有状态的数据中心化环境上扩展智能体强化学习
items.abstract_en: While agentic reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training small language models (SLMs), existing frameworks are predominantly tool-centric and struggle with data-centric environments. Specifically, applying tool-centric frameworks to stateful tasks like SQL debugging introduces severe spatial inefficiencies since proper environment isolation typically requires a separate database container per rollout. Naively reusing databases without tracking evolving states across multi-turn interactions causes trajectory contamination and cross-trajectory interference, which severely destabilizes policy updates. To overcome these bottlenecks, we introduce BIRD-RL, a novel four-stage agentic RL curriculum that alternately enhances foundational agent reasoning and trajectory-adaptive on-policy exploration to circumvent the instability inherently associated with direct end-to-end learning. Crucially, to support this curriculum, BIRD-RL is driven by a Trajectory-scoped Persistent Execution Infrastructure, which enables safe database replica reuse while preserving trajectory isolation. This design improves spatial RL efficiency by 12.8x, successfully enabling scalable agentic RL for complex data-centric tasks without needs of Kubernettes. Empirical evaluations on the BIRD-CRITIC-SQLite benchmark demonstrate that our 7B and 14B models achieve Success Rates of 44.40% and 48.00%, respectively, showing competitive performance against strong proprietary model-based agents such as Claude-Opus-4.6 Agent (48.20%). Furthermore, BIRD-RL successfully trains unified SLMs capable of both advanced SQL debugging and generation, highlighting its broader potential for multi-objective optimization across heterogeneous, real-world data-centric tasks.

items.title_en: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
items.title_zh: RobustRLlib：面向鲁棒强化学习算法的统一库与基准
items.abstract_en: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.
items.comment: Project page, code, and tutorial: https://robustrl-lib.github.io/

items.title_en: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
items.title_zh: DexPort：面向灵巧手数据采集的手持技能接口
items.abstract_en: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.

items.title_en: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
items.title_zh: MiD-VLM：检测与定位图文对中的全局语义错误信息
items.abstract_en: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. We study this problem using DGM4+, a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies. We propose a multimodal model that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA. The model jointly predicts whether an image-caption pair is authentic, identifies the manipulation type, and grounds the misleading caption tokens. On the DGM4+ validation split, the model achieves an F1 score of $0.9679$ for binary authenticity classification. These results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies, while also motivating further work on precise token-level grounding.

items.title_en: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
items.title_zh: 机器人光学相干断层扫描引导的软组织几何建模：面向数据驱动闭环形状控制的三维表示
items.abstract_en: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions. This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, but target-conditioned control requires effective representations of both observed and desired tissue states. In this work, we introduce an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback. We study full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud representations, with or without residual conditioning, using deterministic (Explicit) and generative diffusion (Diffusion) policies. Across 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, OCT-derived 3D representations support both Explicit and Diffusion policies, with performance depending on representation and residual conditioning. Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion, while voxelized point-cloud Explicit with residuals achieves 0.534 mm for depth and 0.443 mm for directional control, with comparable accuracy at intermediate unseen targets and consistent performance across deployments. We further evaluate the framework in 60 ex vivo porcine rollouts, extending to biological tissue with final geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. These results establish volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.

items.title_en: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.title_zh: 初次不成功便回溯：面向冻结VLA的轻量级恢复
items.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.

items.title_en: A Unified Evaluation Framework of Physical Adversarial Robustness in the Edge VLM Era
items.title_zh: 边缘VLM时代的物理对抗鲁棒性统一评估框架
items.abstract_en: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable end-to-end visual grounding via language prompts and generative decoding, demonstrating largely improved zero-shot and open-vocabulary detection capabilities. As a result, VLMs are rapidly being deployed at the edge in safety-critical real-world systems. However, the physical adversarial robustness of edge VLMs has not been systematically studied, and the fundamental differences in output with modern object detectors create methodological challenges for fair evaluation. To compare the two families directly, we evaluate every selected representative model on one outcome: whether an adversarial patch worn on a person evades detection of the model. We report this by introducing a unified metric, conditional attack success rate (cASR), counted only on images the model still localizes under a matched gray occluder, and partition every failure into omission (no box), substitution (a box on the patch), and displacement (a box on neither). We benchmark the physical adversarial vulnerability of compact grounding VLMs against a range of object detectors, and find that the VLMs can be as vulnerable as the detectors. We disclose that failure mode is largely associated with the output format of a model rather than its architecture family. Of the three, only omission is visible to a downstream system; displacement and substitution return confident, well-formed boxes, making them potentially more dangerous failures. Further, we find that, under distribution shift, VLMs that primarily failed by omission instead shift to failing more by displacement/substitution. Thus, a grounding VLM can inherit the detector's vulnerability while showing the possibility to adopt more dangerous failure modes. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/ericliang1/physical-adversarial-robustness.
items.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Grounded and Faithful Vision-Language Models for Real-World Deployment (VLM4RWD). 16 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Code: https://github.com/ericliang1/physical-adversarial-robustness

items.title_en: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
items.title_zh: 正则化RL提升仿真到现实迁移
items.abstract_en: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.
items.comment: 9 pages of main-body content, with supporting details in the appendices. Under submission

items.title_en: CompMVR: Compression-Aware Multi-View Restoration Using Diffusion Models for Geometrically Consistent 3D Reconstruction
items.title_zh: CompMVR：使用扩散模型的压缩感知多视图恢复，用于几何一致的三维重建
items.abstract_en: Real-world 3D reconstruction pipelines often rely on multi-view images degraded by lossy compression. While compression artifacts have been extensively studied in single-image or video restoration, their impact on multi-view geometry remains largely overlooked. In this work, we identify compression-induced cross-view geometric inconsistency as a critical failure mode, where view-dependent artifacts disrupt feature matching, dense correspondence, camera parameter estimation, and downstream 3D reconstruction tasks such as novel view synthesis. To address this problem, we propose CompMVR, a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework that jointly refines compressed views while preserving cross-view consistency, and construct compressed datasets for systematic evaluation. Unlike conventional restoration methods that optimize each image independently for 2D perceptual quality, CompMVR leverages learned compression priors and cross-view correspondence to recover visual details while improving geometric reliability across views. Experiments across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels demonstrate gains in restoration quality and downstream 3D tasks, including novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching. These results establish compressed multi-view restoration as a distinct problem and highlight its importance for 3D reconstruction under lossy compression. Code and data for this paper are available at https://mchaewon.github.io/CompMVR-project-page/.

items.title_en: Predictive Long-Horizon Progress Modeling with Action-Aware Quantification
items.title_zh: 基于动作感知量化的预测性长时程进展建模
items.abstract_en: Quantitative and dense task progress feedback is essential for robotic manipulation across data curation, policy evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Existing progress annotations often rely on sparse keyframe markings derived from subjective manual judgments, limiting their scalability and cross-task consistency, particularly in long-horizon manipulation. To overcome these challenges, we propose action-aware quantification, a unified progress specification that decomposes long-horizon trajectories into object-level subtasks via a vision-language model (VLM) and assigns weighted action credits to capture fine-grained execution dynamics. Using VLM auto-labeling and human calibration, we construct an 800+ hour training video dataset and LOOM, a long-horizon progress benchmark containing 19,618 human-calibrated evaluation frames. To model these dense progress dynamics, we introduce NimCritic, a predictive progress critic trained via Joint Video-Progress Learning. We further incorporate Historical Progress Perturbation to mitigate sequential drift, and design a contrastive Video-Progress Alignment objective that bridges asymmetric expert streams by mutually grounding intermediate visual dynamics and denoised progress trajectories. NimCritic matches or outperforms state-of-the-art process reward models (PRMs) on the established Video Progress Benchmark (VPB) and LOOM, surpassing GVL (GPT-6-Sol) on VPB by about 65% in terminal success accuracy (TSA). On the large-scale RoboArena policy evaluation benchmark, it also retrieves human-selected successful rollouts with about 97% overall recall. These results establish action-aware quantification as a scalable foundation for dense progress feedback in robotic manipulation.

items.title_en: Semantic Representation for Agentic Self-Play in Automated Laboratories
items.title_zh: 自动化实验室中面向智能体自博弈的语义表示
items.abstract_en: Navigating complex, high-dimensional biological search spaces necessitates scalable physical and computational intelligence to explore beyond local optima through iterative self-play across ideation, experimentation, and automation. Translating experimental designs into reliable physical execution remains bottlenecked by static laboratory automation and unmodeled physical variability. To address this, we introduce VERified Infrastructure for Discovery Laboratories, or VERID, a foundational infrastructure designed to bridge the gap between the high-level reasoning of artificial intelligence (AI) agents and complex, error-prone physical realities of wet labs. VERID is a persistent, high-fidelity semantic digital twin of the laboratory workcell that provides four core services: queryable introspection for agentic reasoning, time-compressed simulation for protocol validation, comprehensive trace persistence for a complete scientific record, and a framework for safe execution. We present three case studies using aqueous dye and deionized water mixtures to validate the optical and fluidic foundations of VERID. These studies demonstrate how VERID enables pre-emptive detection of critical errors in experimental protocols, stateful mid-run error recovery and post-hoc identification of subtle physical failures. The simulation functions as a discrete accounting engine, allowing agents to safely and inexpensively explore experimental designs in silico and refine experimental strategies through iterative self-play. VERID also captures structured multimodal experimental data for downstream analysis, knowledge mining and agent training. We argue that this semantic layer is an essential prerequisite for deploying autonomous agents in the biochemical and biomedical sciences, ensuring data integrity, operational safety, and paving the way for tackling previously intractable grand challenges in biology.

items.title_en: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection
items.title_zh: 用于异常识别的自适应世界模型（AWARE）：机器人动力学预测与内省框架
items.abstract_en: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states. However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction. Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation. Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.

rm.usage: 用外部相机+世界模型预测自身动力学并做异常检测，可尝试用于哨兵/雷达端监测机器人卡死、打滑等异常状态，但缺乏电机反馈的假设与RM实际条件不完全吻合。

items.title_en: Are Textual Residuals Truly Complementary? Learning Visual Complements under Semantic Superposition for Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification
items.title_zh: 文本残差真的互补吗？面向可见光-红外行人重识别的语义叠加下视觉互补学习
items.abstract_en: Text-enhanced visible-infrared person re-identification (VI-ReID) exploits textual descriptions to compensate for appearance cues that are weak or unavailable under infrared imaging. Existing methods construct compensation from differences between modality-oriented textual representations, implicitly assuming that textual differences are visually complementary. We revisit this assumption through semantic superposition and show that dense textual residuals may entangle useful appearance variations with redundant, making direct residual fusion unreliable. We propose Superposition-Aware Residual Calibration, which transforms dense textual differences into selective and visually grounded complements. Low-Interference Sparse Residual Learning represents modality-oriented text embeddings as sparse activation strengths over a shared dictionary, selects positive strength differences, and suppresses both dictionary-level overlap and activation-weighted interference to reconstruct a compact, selectively controlled residual. Visual Complement and Counterfactual Calibration further calibrates the residual against identity-specific RGB-IR visual discrepancies, encouraging retained semantics to provide meaningful compensation while preserving the residual structure. Experiments on Tri-SYSU-MM01, Tri-RegDB, and Tri-LLCM show that SARC consistently improves the VI-ReID backbone and remains competitive with text-assisted methods. Mechanism analyses show that SARC produces more concentrated textual variations, reduces dictionary-level feature interference, and improves residual-visual-complement alignment for most samples. These results demonstrate that effective cross-modal compensation requires textual residuals to be selectively represented and explicitly calibrated, rather than directly treated as visual complements. Code and implementation details will be released upon publication.

rm.usage: 可见光-红外行人重识别，主要用于跨模态目标身份保持；RM雷达虽有多目标跟踪与数据关联需求，但缺少红外模态与行人场景，迁移价值低。

items.title_en: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
items.title_zh: 自然语言到Nav2：基于代价地图导航的操作策略
items.abstract_en: Autonomous mobile robots support material transport in warehouses and industrial facilities, where navigation must adapt to changing operating conditions. Sensor observations reveal physical obstacles, but do not by themselves specify temporary access rules, route preferences, or exceptions known to operators. This paper presents a natural-language policy interface that brings this knowledge into ROS 2 Nav2. A local large language model converts instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions. Deterministic checks govern mission acceptance, and three costmap adapters project accepted policies into the existing navigation stack without changing its planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local models produce 107-142 correct accepted policies, compared with 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3-20 incorrect acceptances per model. Fault injection records rejection of eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults. Navigation experiments use correct task policies to evaluate keepouts, zone costs, person-dependent regions, and event-conditioned passage in simulation and on a TurtleBot3. For Tasks 1-3, mean travel times are 18.4-24.5% lower in simulation and 23.1-35.0% lower on the physical testbed than with the baseline lacking those policies. A native KeepoutFilter comparison and two-robot demonstrations examine basic keepout behavior and shared policy projection. The interface connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components.
items.comment: 23 pages, 16 figures, including supplementary material. Jiyeong Chae and Hyunkyo Seo contributed equally. Project page: https://a56239637-dot.github.io/Natural-Language-to-Nav2-Project-Page/

rm.usage: 可让本地LLM把自然语言战术指令转成Nav2代价地图策略（目的地、禁行区、时间条件），用于哨兵自主导航中快速注入路线偏好和临时禁行约束，需适配RM场地地图与裁判系统数据。

items.title_en: Hair Segmentation and Skin Characterization on Macroscopic Dermatological Images for Laser Treatment Parameterization
items.title_zh: 面向激光治疗参数化的宏观皮肤科图像头发分割与皮肤表征
items.abstract_en: Current light-based devices, such as laser hair removal, intense pulsed light (IPL), vascular laser therapy, and dermatologic phototherapy, are widely used in clinical dermatology but rely heavily on subjective manual parameterization or uncalibrated point-based colorimeters. To overcome these limitations, this work presents a unified system for hair segmentation and skin characterization in macroscopic dermatological images. Unlike most existing literature that relies on dermoscopic datasets captured under highly controlled conditions, our approach is specifically designed for macroscopic images that replicate real clinical laser treatments. The proposed pipeline integrates a custom-trained variant of the YOLOv9 deep learning architecture for instance segmentation and classical image processing within a single workflow to extract objective skin and hair parameters such as phototype, hair density, color, and thickness. A color calibration stage using spectrophotometric measurements ensures accurate feature estimation regardless of illumination conditions. Experimental results show competitive segmentation metrics (mAP@50 $\approx$ 0.80) on a custom dataset featuring short, shaved hairs, typical of pre-treatment scenarios. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed pipeline in providing the objective, foundational skin and hair features required for future automated laser parameterization, paving the way for its extension to broader light-based medical therapies.
items.comment: Published open access in Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine (2026)

rm.usage: 面向皮肤科激光治疗参数化的毛发分割与皮肤表征，与RoboMaster的装甲板、能量机关、导航等视觉任务无直接关联，基本用不上。

items.title_en: OWLS: Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields for Zero-Shot Rover Navigation
items.title_zh: OWLS：面向零样本漫游车导航的开放世界语言条件速度场
items.abstract_en: Semantics can provide a proxy for physical traversability. Terrain that looks like loose sand or a rock field is likely to have similar physical properties. Open-vocabulary vision-language models (VLMs) enable this physical reasoning over terrain outside any fixed label set. We present Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields (OWLS), which plans directly over the dense feature map of a VLM. Prompted with a description of traversable terrain, the VLM scores every pixel of a single camera image; OWLS projects these scores onto the ground, adapts them to the platform with two morphological operations, and uses the result as the speed field of a minimum-time planner, so terrain appearance and obstacle clearance shape one trajectory. OWLS needs no task-specific training, no terrain annotation, no persistent map, and no exteroceptive sensor beyond the camera. We evaluate it on a physical rover indoors and off-road, on simulated Mars and Moon rovers over 200 procedurally generated terrains, and on real planetary imagery.

rm.usage: 可用开放词汇VLM对单目图像逐像素评估地形可通行性并生成速度场，为哨兵导航提供语义代价参考；但RM赛场地面平整、结构固定，直接收益有限，更多是异常地形/避障思路参考。

items.abstract_en: These lecture notes provide an introduction to optimization, optimal control, and reinforcement learning for robotics, emphasizing their mathematical connections and practical relevance. They present established material compiled and edited by Yonghyeon Lee, rather than new research results. The notes were developed through a human and AI collaborative writing process, with AI assistance in drafting, organizing, and refining the exposition. This first version is a preliminary collection of notes, not yet a fully developed textbook, and currently contains no figures or graphs. The notes may be revised, corrected, and expanded in future versions.
